item.title: Population-based Prevalence of Bronchiectasis in the United States.
item.author: Iglay ALK, Mingora CM, Mountford WK, Zhang L, Engel AT, Olson AL, Flume PA.
item.description:
Background Bronchiectasis is a chronic, heterogeneous lung disease of rising prevalence; however, contemporary epidemiological data are lacking. Furthermore, paediatric prevalence and cystic fibrosis (CF)-related bronchiectasis prevalence are frequently absent from existing literature. Research question What is the prevalence of bronchiectasis in the United States? Study design and methods This retrospective, observational study utilised data from the Optum® Clinformatics® Data Mart claims database to estimate the age- and sex-standardised prevalence of bronchiectasis in the US in people of all ages and paediatrics (aged < 18 years). Prevalence was stratified by age, sex, ethnicity and insurance coverage. item.title: Subspecialty ILD Clinic Care is Associated with More Guideline-Concordant Evaluation and Improved Outcomes Compared to Other Ambulatory Settings: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.author: Farrand E, Mills H, Radhakrishnan L, Ieong M, Lee A, Gologorskaya O, Butte A.
item.description:
Background Subspecialty interstitial lung disease (ILD) clinics are associated with improved outcomes, yet access remains uneven. Even within tertiary health systems, patients with ILD are managed across diverse ambulatory settings, with unclear implications for care and outcomes. Research question Within a single academic health system, do patient characteristics, care delivery, and outcomes differ between individuals with ILD managed in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus other ambulatory settings? Study design and methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with ILD at a large academic medical center. Identified patients were stratified by care in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus non-specialty setting. item.title: Azithromycin Exposure and Incident Nontuberculous Mycobacterial Isolation in Bronchiectasis and COPD: A Nationwide Nested Case-Control Study.
item.author: Torsheim IL, Wedervang EB, Vognsen AK, Lillebaek T, Fløe A, Dahl VN, Stæhr Jensen JU, Sivapalan P.
item.description:
Background Azithromycin reduces exacerbations in chronic airway disease, but whether it alters the risk of nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) isolation is unresolved. Research question Is azithromycin exposure in the preceding year associated with incident respiratory NTM isolation in non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis and in COPD? Study design and methods Two nationwide register-based nested case-control analyses in Denmark. Case patients had a first positive respiratory culture for NTM; controls, alive and free of prior NTM isolation on the index date, were matched 1:20 on age, sex, and comorbidity index. item.description:
Background The clinical phenotypes, prognosis, and heterogeneity of mild-to-moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have not been systematically evaluated. Research question Do different clinical phenotypes of mild-to-moderate COPD have different prognoses? Study design and methods We analysed the baseline and 3-year follow-up data of participants with mild-to-moderate COPD from a prospective community-based cohort study. Mild-to-moderate COPD was defined as a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV 1 ) / forced vital capacity ratio of < 0.70 and FEV 1 ≥ 50% of the predicted value. item.title: Adherence to Non-Invasive Ventilation in a Provincial Cohort of Children.
item.author: Kendzerska T, Pizzuti R, Talarico R, Gershon AS, Rose L, Amin R.
item.description:
Background Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) adherence is critical to its effectiveness, yet no standardized pediatric definition of "optimal" adherence exists, and population-level data are scarce. Research question What are adherence patterns to NIV in children, and which factors are associated with adherence in a provincial longitudinal cohort? Study design and methods Canadian retrospective longitudinal cohort study linking records from the Ontario Ventilator Equipment Pool to health administrative databases. We identified children < 18 years prescribed NIV with telemonitoring (2020 to 2022) and ≥1 month of data. The adherence definitions explored were the adult definition of ≥4 hours/day (primary) and measures of any daily use, daily NIV hours, and data missingness ("days not used" = 0 hours recorded; "days no data" = no signal). item.description:
Background Less-invasive, lower-risk alternatives to surgical lung biopsy (SLB) have emerged for interstitial lung disease (ILD) diagnosis, such as transbronchial lung cryobiopsy (TBLC) and Envisia Genomic Classifier (EGC), but suffer from limited sampling and simplified binomial classification, respectively. Endobronchial optical coherence tomography (EB-OCT) is a low-risk, large-volume bronchoscopic imaging modality with microscopic resolution, which accurately detects features and patterns for ILD diagnosis as previously validated against SLB. Research question How does EB-OCT contribute to ILD diagnosis and diagnostic confidence at multidisciplinary discussion (MDD) when paired with clinically indicated TBLC and EGC? item.title: Determinants of lung cancer screening follow-up care in community care settings: A qualitative multi-case study in the ACCELL trial.
item.author: Palazzo L, Hansell L, Wernli KJ, Brown M, Snidarich M, Louie T, Long S, Walsh C, Coronado GD, DeCell Arnp K, Lodhi S, Leone RJ, Wysham N, Triplette M.
item.description:
Background Adherence to lung cancer screening (LCS) follow-up is essential to achieve mortality benefits from screening. However, population-based studies demonstrate follow-up is < 50% in clinical settings. Determinants (barriers and facilitators) of LCS follow-up in community settings are under-studied. Research question What are determinants of LCS follow-up in community settings? Study design and methods This qualitative multi-case study informed a pre-post intervention trial, testing pragmatic interventions to address LCS follow-up in community settings. item.title: Dyspnea during resting breathing and carbon dioxide rebreathing in adult patients with congenital central hypoventilation syndrome.
item.author: Bret M, Laveneziana P, Niérat MC, Lavault S, Patout M, Zaien I, Teulier M, Bianquis C, Straus C, Morélot-Panzini C, Similowski T.
item.description:
Background Congenital central hypoventilation syndrome (CCHS) is an ultra-rare genetic disorder caused by PHOX2B mutations. Patients lack central CO2 chemosensitivity and require ventilatory support during sleep. Children with CCHS have been reported to lack CO2-induced air hunger, but respiratory sensations and dyspnea have not been characterized in adults. item.author: Milinic T, Kelley JG, Whikehart SM, Anand A, Knapp SC, Brandon W, Turner GA, Serna D, Lechtzin N, Tupayachi Ortiz MG, Kapnadak SG, Dunitz JM, Saavedra MT, Taylor-Cousar JL, Brown CE, Goss CH, Ramos KJ.
item.description:
Background Black and Hispanic people with cystic fibrosis (PwCF) experience worse health outcomes. Health disparities are exacerbated by clinical research that does not adequately represent the diversity of the CF population. Research questions How do Black/African American and Hispanic/Latino(a) PwCF perceive clinical research? What are the barriers and facilitators to participation in research? Are there viable solutions to improve inclusion?
